chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Yusuf al-Baghdadi narrated that Ali ibn Anbasa said: 'Abu al-Hasan Bakr ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ziyad ibn Musa ibn Malik al-Ashja'i al-Asri narrated to me: Fatima, daughter of Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon him), narrated to us: I heard my father Ali narrating from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father and his uncle Zayd, from their father Ali ibn Al-Husayn, from his father and his uncle, from Abu Talib (peace be upon him).'
He said: 'It is not permissible for a Muslim to scare another Muslim.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on causing fear to another Muslim in Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith traces its chain back to the Ahl al-Bayt, establishing the prohibition of *irwa'* (causing fear or anxiety) as a fundamental social right. It underscores the Imamate’s role in cultivating psychological security (*aman*) within the community, ensuring that interactions are free from distress or intimidation.
